title: Cornell president calls gang rape allegations 'deeply disturbing'
description: Cornell president Michael I. Kotlikoff said his university "must do better" in a video statement. "This is a defining moment in Cornell's history," he added.

title: U.S. Marine arrested for alleged murder of a woman in Okinawa, Japan
description: Japanese police arrested a U.S. Marine in the alleged robbery and murder of a woman on Okinawa, officials said Sunday.

title: How the Cornell case is affecting women who have experienced sexual assault
description: The rape allegations that have emerged from a Cornell University frat house are leading many women to remember their own experiences — and call for a wider reckoning over sexual violence.

title: She died covering war for Fox News. Her parents blame the network — and a star reporter
description: The family members of two Fox News journalists killed while covering the war in Ukraine are suing the network, saying it put getting the story ahead of its people.

title: Latter-day Saints women turn away from scandal-plagued Republican candidate in Arizona
description: Arizona Republican candidate for Congress Mark Lamb has been accused of sexual misconduct while sheriff. His controversy is turning many voters away as Democrats see an opportunity in the red seat.

title: Coast Guard finds debris from medical plane carrying 6 people
description: Flight data shows the jet dropped at least 9,000 feet over two minutes, then leveled off for several more minutes, before disappearing.

title: Can the Cornell lawsuit force changes that make students safer?
description: Universities have responsibilities when students report sexual assault, even if prosecutors don't bring charges. Attorney Baine Kerr explains how those protections work.

title: Opinion: A Hawk is not the same as a Hawkeye
description: This was emphasized to people watching a Senate hearing this week, where confusion over two basketball teams was on display.

title: Economist Betsey Stevenson breaks down the gender gap in recent hiring reports
description: The U.S. economy added fewer jobs than expected last month and unemployment ticked up to 4.2%. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Betsey Stevenson, an economist at the University of Michigan.

title: All's fair in love and 'War' — a well-cast, classy-trashy divorce drama
description: HBO's War is intended to be an anthology series about two dueling London law firms. The first season stars Dominic West and Sienna Miller as a high-profile couple in the midst of a very nasty divorce.

title: For some Brazilians, this election is a vote on Trump
description: President Trump says he's been having success winning races in Latin America. As Brazilian voters go to the polls, they're also deciding how much influence Trump should have in their country.

title: France arrests 5,000 people, mostly teens, as school protests spread
description: High school students say their classrooms are overcrowded, teachers are missing and buildings need repairs. The protests have spread to cities across France, and some 5,000 people have been arrested.

title: U.S. withdrawal from Iraq is complete
description: Twenty-three years after President George W. Bush's campaign of "shock and awe," the U.S. military has completed its withdrawal from Iraq.

title: Lula or Bolsonaro? Some Brazilian voters say they don't want either
description: Brazil's election enters its final day of campaigning as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro make their last pitches to voters. Brazilians explain what worries them, and why some still can't choose.

title: Brazil's big political rematch: What to know about the Brazilian election
description: Four years after President Lula narrowly defeated Jair Bolsonaro, Brazil is back at the ballot box. This time, Lula faces Bolsonaro's son, Flávio, in a high-stakes rematch.

title: How Brazil's two leading presidential candidates are talking about crime
description: Crime is at the top of voters' concerns in Brazil ahead of Sunday's national elections. Many are calling for tougher measures — part of a broader rightward shift across Latin America.

title: The G7 will release 100 million reserve barrels of diesel fuel over the next 4 months
description: After increased pressure from Washington, the G7 held an emergency meeting on energy. The world's wealthiest nations say they will release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel fuel in their reserves.

title: Germany's political center fights for relevance after far-right and far-left gains
description: Centrist politicians are soul-searching after electoral gains by the far right and the far left. Today's weak coalitions, political fragmentation and dire economy echo a past that led to the rise of fascism.

title: The U.S. added only 29,000 jobs in September as job market lacks spark
description: U.S. employers added 29,000 jobs in September as the unemployment rate inched up to 4.2%. Job gains for July and August were revised down by a total of 60,000 jobs, extending a lackluster run for the job market.

title: Why is diesel more expensive than regular gas?
description: Diesel hasn't always been more expensive than other gasoline. Then in 2004, a switch happened due to air quality standards, demand, and taxes. In this week's Indicator newsletter, we dig into diesel prices, what kind of fun people are buying, and other forms of making your tax bill smaller.

title: U.S. employers add only 29,000 jobs in September, much less than August
description: The Labor Department offered an update Friday on the strength of the U.S. job market. The news comes as long-term interest rates have been climbing.

title: Economist discusses high bond yields and the September jobs report
description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks to Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's Analytics, about high bond yields and the September jobs report.

title: Some of the super wealthy are plowing money into a tax loophole to slash taxes to 0
description: There's a tax loophole that lets millionaires and billionaires drawdown their taxes… to nothing. So what does tax-loss harvesting mean and why is it still allowed?

title: The rising cost of borrowing piles more financial pressure onto consumers
description: Mortgage rates are at their highest level in almost three years. The rising cost of borrowing is driving life's major purchases further out of reach.

title: Trade tensions mean fewer Canadians flocking to South Florida
description: This South Florida community is typically a refuge for Canadians fleeing cold weather, but trade tensions between the United States and Canada mean fewer are coming.

title: The poverty rate among older Americans is rising, survey shows
description: Bucking the national trend, poverty has been steadily rising among seniors and older adults. A new survey sheds light on how low-income people are struggling in the crucial years before retirement.

title: Mortgage rates break past 7% as bond yields surge, deepening U.S. housing gridlock
description: Bond yields rose this week pushing mortgage rates above 7 percent. That's another big challenge for the already limping US housing market.
